rooms.name: Maintenance Rite Chapel
rooms.instance_premise: The chapel was built to process bodies through a maintenance sequence: kneel, receive, drain. A Warden—an enforcement organism grown to keep the sequence running after the original workers were replaced—is still active and treats posture as compliance or violation. Hymn has entered upright. The Warden has already turned. It does not distinguish refusal from intrusion. The kneel channels, drain gutter, and tool-rest larvae are all live infrastructure, not decoration. The Warden uses grip and leverage to force compliance; it was built for that, not for killing. Whether Hymn kneels, fights, or fakes the sequence, the chapel leaves a drain-residue outcome and a Warden wound state.
rooms.first_visit_description: The floor is grooved hip-to-drain in channels worn smooth by weight, not tools. Tool-rest larvae line the walls at grip height, each one shaped open, each one waiting. The drain cuts run from every kneel point to a central gutter that is still wet. A Warden stands at the far end: dense, low-slung, built like a body that learned to enforce by watching the sequence break. It has already turned toward me. It reads stance. Mine is wrong.
rooms.return_description: The kneel channels are dry. The Warden's station is empty. The tool-rest larvae hold open at grip height, patient and unchanged.

corpus_influences.writing_influence: The Warden enforces through grip and posture correction, not killing. Its enforcement model has a structural blind side: it cannot grip what it cannot reach, and it cannot reach what is already inside its line.
corpus_influences.scenario_application: Shapes the combat choice as a pre-emption of grip, the compliance choice as a body-cost submission, and the fake-sequence choice as a route through the Warden's commitment window. All three choices are readable as tactical posture decisions, not puzzle inputs.

rooms.instance_premise: A shallow glow pool holds motile repair threads that respond to open wounds. A custodian organism crouches at the far rim, already feeding a rival patient whose injuries are worse than Hymn's. The custodian controls entry by wound priority and will treat any body that uses the pool without consent as a parasite rather than a patient.

It is feeding a second body already half-submerged, one arm trailing, breathing in shallow pulls. The custodian does not look up but its scent-fans open toward me the moment I cross the threshold. The rim bone is worn smooth. The threads are already moving my direction.

rooms.name: Egg Corridor
rooms.instance_premise: A transit vein narrowed by brood-growth where one sac has already opened. The hatchling is present, injured, and watching. The lane's cilia react to heat and breath. Hymn's choice of witness, mercy, or passage determines which brood-line follow-up follows her out.

A feeder valve at knee height opens on my heat and pushes sweet air up my front. One sac to my right has already split. The hatchling is still inside the lower half of the shell, one forelimb hooked over the lip, the other folded wrong under its body. It is not moving toward me. It is watching me. Its eye membrane is still wet. The drag ridges on the floor go nowhere: it has not left yet. The intact sacs around it have tightened. They are reading what I do next.
rooms.return_description: The brood lane again. The split shell is dry now, its lip curled back. The drag ridges are older but still readable. The intact sacs loosen slightly when I enter, then hold.

The corridor smells sweet and close, like a wound that has been sealed too long. He has not turned around yet, but his shoulders have changed.
rooms.return_description: The plaque is dark. Silt's cord is still looped around the anchor blister near the floor seam. He has been back.

rooms.first_visit_description: The red corridor pinches into a chapel pocket three strides wide. The walls carry tendon cuts that open, close, and open again in a rhythm I can feel through my boot soles. Amar Creepstride stands in the middle stride with his saw held low at wrist height, blade angled so my arm has to cross it to reach the seam. Behind me the corridor shudders. Something heavy is testing the passage with its teeth. Amar watches my feet. He is deciding whether I step like prey.
rooms.return_description: The red chapel pocket holds its three-beat wall rhythm and Amar's absence or presence depending on what I left here.

corpus_influences.source_moment: A hunter closes a corridor while a dangerous figure waits at the only exit, forcing the protagonist to commit to violence or be caught between two threats.
corpus_influences.writing_influence: The hunter behind Hymn and Amar at the seam recreate the corridor-trap structure: two threats, one narrow space, no neutral ground.
corpus_influences.scenario_application: The hunter's approach is the ticking clock. Amar's saw position is the gate. Every choice is shaped by the fact that doing nothing is the worst option.

corpus_influences.source_moment: A skilled swordsman teaches a student under conditions of mutual suspicion and unequal power, where the student must decide how much to owe the teacher and whether the debt is worth the skill.
corpus_influences.writing_influence: Amar's offer of saw-timing discipline is the teaching-under-debt structure. The debt is concrete and collectible, not abstract gratitude.
corpus_influences.scenario_application: The cooperative branch creates a real obligation Amar can call in. The resentment branch mirrors the student who watches and copies without paying, which Sabatini frames as a specific kind of betrayal that instructors remember.

corpus_influences.source_moment: The environment has a pulse that the characters can either attune to or be destroyed by. Attunement requires surrender of some autonomy. Resistance is fatal.
corpus_influences.writing_influence: The three-beat wall rhythm is not decoration. It is the room's active system. Reading it correctly is survival. Misreading it costs flesh.
corpus_influences.scenario_application: The wall rhythm is the room's body. All three branches require Hymn to interact with it differently: Amar teaches the read, Hymn steals the read, or Hymn forces through without the read and pays a wound cost.

animal_infrastructure.function: Closes on a three-beat tendon rhythm and punishes any body that enters without matching weight, wrist angle, and timing.
Vents scent and pressure into the hunter lane; cut correctly, it blinds pursuit for one beat; cut badly, it calls the hunter closer.
A practical red-corridor fighting method: set the wrist, read the wall-opening rhythm, cut the line, recover before the seam bites.

cross_run_story_hooks: If Hymn learns the saw timing, later red corridors can offer wall-opening choices without Amar present.
If Hymn kills Amar, hunter rooms can treat the noisy route as a rival-predator signal rather than lost-prey drift.
If Hymn repeatedly uses Amar as cover, red corridor endings can pull toward debt to Amar instead of clean body mastery.
environment_echoes: Later corridors with timed wall cuts will be easier if Hymn learned the read here, harder if she only copied it once, and neutral if she killed Amar and took the route alone.
Amar's debt receipt blister appears in a later room as a collectible pressure if the cooperative branch was taken.
Hunter scent in seams becomes a recurring recognition tag if Hymn was caught in the corridor rhythm here.

mutation_hooks.baseline_route: Hymn reads the wall rhythm by feel through her boots and times her crossing on the third beat without help. She takes a glancing cut from Amar's saw if her timing is off by half a stride.
mutation_hooks.mutation_branch: Lean Muscle lets Hymn cross the seam before Amar can reset his saw position, turning his timing advantage into a gap she can exploit without learning the rhythm.
mutation_hooks.symbiote_branch: Impermeable Barrier lets Hymn take Amar's saw contact without flinching, which changes his read of her and opens a negotiation beat that the baseline route does not have.
mutation_hooks.effect: Speed mutation removes the timing requirement but not the debt or resentment structure. Barrier mutation adds a social branch.
mutation_hooks.in_encounter_use: Cross the seam before Amar's saw can track the movement.
mutation_hooks.out_of_encounter_use: Pass timed-wall corridors in later rooms without needing to read the rhythm.
mutation_hooks.surprising_second_use: Outrun the hunter's corridor approach long enough to make Amar's offer irrelevant.

progression_state.early: Hymn is learning that the organism has rhythms that can be read. Amar is the first person who treats that reading as a tradeable skill.
progression_state.mid: The debt or resentment from this room returns as leverage. Amar either calls the debt or acts on the resentment depending on which branch was taken.
progression_state.late: Hymn's relationship to timed-wall corridors is shaped by what she did here. The route remembers.
